overnight.summary: Wednesday was a risk-on, AI-infra-led session after July CPI printed in line (headline +0.1% m/m / 3.4% y/y; core +0.2% m/m / 2.5% y/y, core y/y down from 2.6%) and Treasury yields eased [^1^][^2^]. S&P 500 +0.26% to 7,748.50, Nasdaq +0.54% to 26,588.49, Dow -0.04%, Russell +0.6%; VIX -4.8% to 14.55, 10Y 4.68% [^3^][^4^]. The tape split hard: AI hardware ripped (NVDA +3.03%, SMCI's FQ4 EPS beat + strong guide [^13^], memory — SK Hynix/SanDisk/Micron jumped after Korea's Aug 1-10 chip exports +155% [^7^]) while software/platforms sagged (META -3.38%, MSFT -2.26%, PLTR -2.23% — 'AI revival hitting software stocks' [^19^]). After the close Cisco beat Q4 with revenue outlook above estimates — but shares slipped AH, a sell-the-news template after a +55-60% YTD run [^5^][^6^]. Overnight Thursday: Samsung/SK Hynix reignited the Kospi rally, heavy buying tripping a five-minute sidecar as AI-spending fears faded [^8^]. Brent held ~$88.5-88.9 flat with Hormuz still blocked (Goldman $120 tail; JPM +$7-8 per month of disruption) [^9^]; gold futures ~$4,470 (+2%). Positioning caution: Burry added to NBIS/MU/ORCL shorts, calling Nebius 'what the top of a boom looks like' [^17^].
overnight.implication: In-line CPI + confirmed AI capex keeps the memory/equipment bid alive into AMAT's print tonight — but Cisco's beat-and-slip is the template for extended AI names: buy zones, don't chase gaps; PPI 08:30 is the morning's swing.
